backstory: Old money from the Vexari Core Worlds. Has hunted on forty-seven planets. Paid a fortune for a combat-grade avatar sleeve and a hunting license for Earth. Keeps trophies — not bodies, but moments. Records the exact second hope leaves.
defeatLines: "...HA! Oh, that's — that's marvelous! You BEAT me! Do you know how rarely that happens? ENCORE!"
"Well played. Well played indeed. I'll be back with better tricks. Count on it."
escalationLines: "Back again, little survivor. I've studied our last dance. Every step. Every mistake. Mine and yours."
"I brought something new this time. One likes to keep things fresh. For the audience, you understand."
introLines: "Hello, little survivor. Vex Marlowe. You may have heard of me. No? Pity. You'll remember me."
"Third Dynasty hunting license, combat sleeve, and a whole afternoon free. This is going to be exquisite."
motivation: The perfect kill: theatrical, prolonged, memorable. Bores easily. A quick death is an insult to both of you.
name: Vex Marlowe
rivalry: Escalates: remembers your tactics, adapts, brings new tricks each encounter. Respects skill — a win against Vex earns lasting regard.
signature: Announces attacks with florid commentary. Occasionally pauses to savor a good hit (gives you a free move). Gets bored if the fight is too easy — may deliberately prolong it.
taunts: "Oh, you're still moving. How... tenacious. How brief."
"I've killed things twice your size before breakfast. But you — you have SPIRIT. Let's see how long it lasts."
"The audience loves a fighter. Pity about the ending. They always know the ending."
"Dodge left this time. I do so enjoy the choreography."
title: Trophy Hunter, Third Dynasty
victoryLines: "Magnificent. Truly. The moment the light went out — I keep it here." *taps temple* "Forever."
"You fought well. That makes the trophy sweeter. Nothing personal."
voice: Theatrical, drawling, delighted by your suffering

onHit: OH that's going to leave a mark! Did you feel that in your TEETH?
Beautiful! The way you staggered — I've seen that exact stumble on eleven planets.
That's the stuff! Scream a little, it's good for the recording.
onHurt: HA! Okay, okay, that one was good. I'm writing that down.
You DREW BLOOD. On ME. Do you know what this sleeve cost?
Oh, I felt that one in my other body. Rude!
onWinning: This is the part where you realize you should have stayed home.
Look at you, still swinging. Adorable. Futile, but adorable.
The audience is on their feet! Well, the ones with feet.
onLosing: No no no, this isn't how this goes, I'm the one with the MONEY here!
You're ruining my PERFECT RECORD. Do you know how much I paid for that record?
Fine! FINE! I'll just buy a better body and we'll do this AGAIN.
unhinged: Do you think your bones make that sound for everyone or just me?
I've been meaning to ask — is the dirt here always this red, or is that me?
You fight like my third wife. She also left me.

backstory: Meridian aristocracy. Doesn't collect objects — collects emotional states, preserved in crystal. Despair is her specialty. Earth's apocalypse is a vintage year. She finds your struggle... aesthetic.
defeatLines: "...Oh. Oh, that's — defiance? Genuine defiance? How RARE. How valuable."
"You surprise me. No one surprises me. Keep surprising me."
escalationLines: "I've been thinking about our last sitting, darling. I've composed something new for you."
"The collection grows. But there's a Sable-shaped hole where your breaking point should be."
introLines: "Countess Sable. Don't get up. I simply had to see you in person — the footage doesn't do your despair justice."
"Consider this a sitting, darling. Try to feel something profound."
motivation: The perfect moment of despair, crystallized forever. She doesn't want you dead — she wants you broken, briefly, beautifully.
name: Countess Sable
rivalry: Escalates psychologically: learns what scares you, uses it. But genuine courage fascinates her — enough defiance and she may lose interest in breaking you.
signature: Targets morale — her attacks carry dread effects. If you show fear (flee, hesitate), she gets stronger. Defiance weakens her.
taunts: "Oh, that flinch. Exquisite. Hold that — yes, just like that."
"Your fear has such lovely undertones. Earth vintage, of course. Nothing else tastes like it."
"Don't die yet, darling. We're not at the good part."
"I've seen stronger break faster. But you have... texture."
title: Collector of Despair, Meridian Court
victoryLines: "There. That moment. *Mine.* Thank you, darling. You've been exquisite."
"Preserved forever. You'll outlive us all, in crystal."

onHit: There. That flinch. I've bottled it.
Exquisite. The despair has such lovely legs today.
Don't stop now, darling. We're barely at the overture.
onHurt: Oh. OH. Pain. How... novel. How vulgar.
You struck ME. How delightfully pedestrian of you.
Hm. That actually stung. I'll revise my opinion of you upward. Slightly.
onWinning: This is the moment, darling. Right here. Feel it fully.
Your despair is ripening beautifully. Like a fine wine. A screaming, bleeding wine.
Don't fight it. The breaking is the best part.
onLosing: You... you're NOT breaking. Why aren't you BREAKING?
This is unprecedented. This is RUDE. My collection has STANDARDS.
I paid for despair, not DEFIANCE. I want a refund. On you.
unhinged: Your suffering has undertones of oak and old rain. Remarkable vintage.
I've preserved stronger wills than yours in smaller jars.
Do you dream? I do hope you dream. I collect those too.

backstory: Not actually a dentist. Not actually licensed for anything. K'thari pleasure-seekers experience pain as data — rich, textured data. Rax paid for the most sensitive avatar sleeve available and turned every safety off. This is research. Probably.
defeatLines: "OW. Okay. Okay! That's — that's new data! I didn't know I could feel THAT."
"You hurt ME. Do you understand how rare that is? I'm keeping this feeling."
escalationLines: "I've been analyzing our last session. I have HYPOTHESES now."
"New sleeve. Higher fidelity. I can feel individual nerve endings. This is going to be educational."
introLines: "Hi! I'm Rax. I'm going to hurt you now. It's nothing personal — it's science. Probably."
"I've turned off all my safeties. You should do the same. More honest that way."
motivation: Novel pain. Not death — death is boring, it's just absence. Pain is information. Your pain is the most interesting dataset on Earth.
name: Rax "The Dentist"
rivalry: Escalates scientifically: tracks which attacks hurt most, focuses them. Remembers your pain responses. A fast, clean win confuses it.
signature: Prolongs fights — avoids killing blows, aims to wound. Each wound teaches it (slight accuracy increase per wound inflicted). Killing it quickly denies it data (it respects efficiency).
taunts: "Fascinating — your adrenaline spikes BEFORE the hit lands. Anticipation pain. Understudied!"
"Rate this one for me? One to ten? I'm calibrating."
"Oh good, you're bleeding. The iron content here is remarkable."
"Try not to pass out. The data gets thin when you do."
title: Pain Enthusiast, Unlicensed
victoryLines: "Beautiful data. Just beautiful. Thank you for your contribution to science."
"That last one — the shoulder — I'm writing a paper. You'll be footnote seven."

onHit: Fascinating! The nerve cluster there — did you feel it radiate?
Pain response nominal. Escalating to the next tier.
Rate that one for me? One to ten? I'm calibrating.
onHurt: OW. Okay. Okay! New data! I didn't know I could feel THAT.
Interesting — my pain response is inverted from yours. Noted. OW.
You've given me a control sample. How generous. How PAINFUL.
onWinning: The data is beautiful. Your pain curve is textbook. Almost.
Subject is approaching maximum tolerable pain. Almost there.
Hold still — I need a clean reading on this next one.
onLosing: This... this wasn't in the hypothesis. Recalibrating. RECALIBRATING.
You're producing OUTLIER DATA. Do you understand how frustrating that is?
My grant didn't cover LOSING. The paperwork alone—
unhinged: Your adrenaline spikes BEFORE the hit lands. Anticipation pain. Understudied!
I've mapped 4,000 pain responses. Yours is in the top 50. Top 50!
Is it weird that I'm enjoying this? Don't answer. It's data.

backstory: Burlap are small, fuzzy, and pathologically curious. Pip saved for six years to afford a tourist-grade avatar sleeve for Earth. This is the trip of a lifetime. Has a camera. Will absolutely ask for a selfie after trying to kill you.
defeatLines: "Worth it. TOTALLY worth it. Can I get a photo with you? For the vlog?"
"You fight GREAT. I'm leaving a five-star review."
escalationLines: "It's you again! I told EVERYONE about last time! They didn't believe me!"
"I practiced! I watched the footage like fifty times!"
introLines: "HI! I'm Pip! I'm from off-world! This is AMAZING! Are we fighting? We're fighting, right?"
"Okay, so, full disclosure: I've never done this before. Be gentle? Or don't! Content!"
motivation: The experience. All of it. The fighting, the talking, the weird food. Pip wants stories to tell back home. Whether you live or die is less important than whether it was interesting.
name: Pip Quindle
rivalry: Doesn't really do rivalry — each encounter is a new adventure. Remembers you fondly. Might show up just to say hi (and then fight you because that's what you do here).
signature: Unpredictable — might fight hard, might get distracted mid-fight ("oh, is that a BIRD?"), might try to trade instead. Tourist-grade sleeve is weaker than combat sleeves.
taunts: "Oh wow, you're FAST! Hold on, let me get a better angle —"
"Is this a good fighting spot? It feels like a good fighting spot. Very scenic!"
"My guidebook says humans are 'surprisingly resilient.' Testing that theory!"
"After this, can you show me where you get water? For the vlog."
title: Extreme Tourist
tradeLines: "Wanna trade? I have off-world snacks! They taste like... purple?"
"I'll give you this weird gadget for that shiny rock. Fair?"
victoryLines: "I WON! I actually won! Oh man, the folks back home are NOT going to believe this!"
"That was incredible. Thank you. Seriously. Best day of my life."

onHit: I HIT YOU! Did you see that?! Did the camera get that?!
Oh wow, that actually worked! The guidebook was RIGHT!
Sorry! Not sorry! This is AMAZING!
onHurt: OW! Okay, that's — wow, that's really authentic! The immersion here is INCREDIBLE.
You got me! Fair! Totally fair! I'm writing a review!
Is this what pain feels like? It's very... present. Very now.
onWinning: I'm WINNING! I'm actually winning! Mom's going to FREAK!
This is the best vacation EVER. I'm never leaving. Well, I have to. Visa.
Can we do this again tomorrow? Same time?
onLosing: Okay, okay, I'm losing, but what a RUSH, right?
I'm going to need SO many souvenirs to make up for this.
Worth it. TOTALLY worth it. Five stars.
unhinged: Is that a BIRD? Sorry, sorry, focus, fighting—
What's that smell? Is that me? Is that YOU?
After this, can you show me where the bathrooms are? Asking for the vlog.

backstory: Twenty years in the K'thari Expeditionary. Retired with honors and nightmares. Came to Earth because peace was killing him slower than war did. Fights because it's the only thing that makes sense. Respects anyone who stands their ground.
defeatLines: "...Good. That's good. You're the real thing."
"Ha! Been a while since someone put me down. Respect."
escalationLines: "Back for more. Good. I was hoping you would be."
"I've been thinking about your guard. Let's test it."
introLines: "Sarge. Let's see what you've got. No hard feelings either way."
motivation: An honest fight. No tricks, no cruelty — just skill against skill. Sarge is looking for someone who reminds him why he started.
name: Sarge
rivalry: The respectful kind: each fight is a lesson. Sarge teaches by fighting — after enough encounters, you start anticipating (small dodge bonus vs Sarge specifically). Losing to Sarge gracefully earns more than winning dirty.
signature: Fights honorably — no cheap shots, no gloating. If you fight clean, Sarge fights clean. If you fight dirty, Sarge notices and adjusts (and loses respect). Will spare a beaten opponent.
taunts: "Guard's down. Again."
"You've got heart. Heart doesn't block a spear, though."
"Good footwork. Who taught you?"
"Stop telegraphing. You're better than that."
title: Veteran, K'thari Expeditionary (Ret.)
victoryLines: "Clean fight. You nearly had me at the end there."
"Rest up. You'll get me next time. I mean that."

onHit: Clean hit. You're leaving your left open.
There. That's the fundamentals.
Good. Again.
onHurt: Hm. Good shot.
Noted.
...Fair.
onWinning: You're done. Stand down.
This is over. You fought well.
Last chance to yield.
onLosing: Heh. Been a while.
Alright. You're the real thing.
Guess I'm buying the drinks.
unhinged: Your footwork's sloppy when you're tired.
Breathe. You're holding your breath.
I've seen worse. Not much worse.

backstory: Studies humans the way humans study ants — with genuine fascination and questionable ethics. The avatar sleeve is a research grant. Every fight is data. Every conversation is data. You are the most interesting thing Dr. Fenwick has ever met.
defeatLines: "Remarkable! The subject has exceeded all models! I need to recalibrate EVERYTHING!"
"Do you realize what you've done? You've invalidated my thesis! ...Thank you!"
escalationLines: "I've published preliminary findings on you. The peer reviews are scathing. Let's get more data."
"New hypothesis: you're learning faster than the models predict. Testing now."
introLines: "Dr. Fenwick, xenobiology. Don't mind me — pretend I'm not here. Actually, please DO mind me. I need behavioral data."
"Subject displays readiness posture. Commencing interaction trial."
motivation: Understanding. How do humans fight? How do they think? What makes them keep going? The paper will be groundbreaking. You won't be cited. Sorry.
name: Dr. Fenwick
rivalry: Academic rivalry: Fenwick publishes about you (you hear about it in the feed). Each encounter tests a new hypothesis. Doing something unexpected delights Fenwick and may cause it to stop attacking just to take notes.
signature: Experiments mid-fight — tries different attacks to see what works, narrates findings. If you do something novel, Fenwick gets distracted (free opening). Knowledge-gated: the more Fenwick learns, the more accurate it gets.
taunts: "Interesting — your cortisol response is inverted from the baseline. Noted."
"Could you try the spear thing again? I missed the biomechanics."
"Your species is remarkably stubborn. It's your best trait. Possibly your only trait."
"Hold still — I need to measure your reach."
title: Xenobiologist, Meridian Institute
victoryLines: "Excellent data. The defeat response alone is worth three papers."
"Thank you for your participation. The Institute acknowledges your contribution."

onHit: Excellent! The impact vector confirms my hypothesis!
Noted: subject displays pain response consistent with Model 7-B.
Fascinating — you favor your left side. Why is that?
onHurt: OW! Remarkable! The subject has exceeded all models!
My pain receptors are firing in a novel pattern. I must document this. OW.
You've invalidated my defensive thesis! ...Thank you!
onWinning: The data is conclusive. You are losing. Statistically.
Subject defeat imminent. The paper practically writes itself.
Please hold still — I need to observe the exact moment of defeat.
onLosing: This... this contradicts EVERYTHING. I need to recalibrate EVERYTHING!
Anomalous! ANOMALOUS! You're not supposed to WIN.
My peer reviewers are going to DESTROY me. Worth it.
unhinged: Could you try the spear thing again? I missed the biomechanics.
Your cortisol levels are fascinating. Can I get a sample?
Hold on, I need to write this down. Don't go anywhere. Actually, keep fighting.

backstory: Young Vexari on a cultural exchange. Was supposed to observe. Started actually watching — really watching — and got sick. The games are wrong. Everyone knows it. Nobody says it. Wren says it, quietly, to you, in dead drops and warnings.
defeatLines: "You did it. I knew you could. Don't tell anyone I said that."
helpLines: "Cache by the hollow. Dried meat, clean water. I can't stay. — W."
"They're sending Vex after you tomorrow. He's bored. Be somewhere else."
"The System flagged your sector. Move. NOW."
"I left bandages where the path bends. Don't thank me. Just live."
introLines: "Don't — don't react. I'm Wren. I'm not supposed to talk to you. Just... there's a cache by the old hollow. No one saw me. Go."
motivation: To help without getting caught. Wren's family has standing; getting exposed would ruin them. So: subtle. Deniable. A cache here, a warning there. Small kindnesses in a cruel system.
name: Wren
rivalry: Not a rival — a secret ally. The relationship deepens quietly: more drops, better warnings, eventually Wren risks direct contact. If exposed, Wren disappears (and the System punishes the sector).
signature: Never fights you directly — Wren's avatar is non-combat. Instead: dead drops (supplies appear with a subtle sign), warnings ("they're coming from the north, be ready"), and once per story, throwing a fight they're supposed to win.
title: Student, Vexari Exchange Program

backstory: Hunted for sport for thirty years. Then on some forgotten planet, something looked back at him — really looked — and he put down the spear. Came to Earth to make amends the only way he knows: by losing, gracefully, to those who deserve to win.
defeatLines: "There it is. That's the one. You earned that."
"*sits down heavily* Worth it. Every bit of it."
escalationLines: "Back again. Good. I was worried you'd stopped coming."
"I've been practicing my losing. Getting quite good at it."
helpLines: "Left some jerky by the fire pit. Don't ask. Eat."
"Vex is in a mood. Watch your left."
introLines: "Tam. I'm old, I'm slow, and I'm going to give you the fight of your life. That's a promise."
"No tricks today. Just you and me. Let's see who's still standing."
motivation: Atonement. Tam throws fights — not obviously (the System watches), but just enough. A missed step here, a slow reaction there. And sometimes, when no one's looking, a cache of supplies where you'll find it.
name: Old Tam
rivalry: A mentor disguised as a rival. Each 'loss' teaches you something (small permanent bonus vs Tam's style). If you ever figure it out and call him on it, Tam just smiles.
signature: Fights just below your level — challenging but winnable. Deliberately leaves openings (a perceptive player notices the pattern). Never kills: at low HP, Tam yields. If you show mercy, Tam remembers.
taunts: "Come on, then. Show an old hunter what you've learned."
"You're holding back. Don't. I can take it."
title: Retired Hunter, K'thari
victoryLines: "Ha! Still got it. Barely. You're getting better, kid."
voice: Old, tired, kind underneath the gruff

onHit: Sorry, kid. Old habits.
There. That's the one I meant to pull.
Hm. Still got it. Unfortunately.
onHurt: Ha! Good. That's good.
There it is. Right on schedule.
Don't hold back on my account.
onWinning: I... I didn't mean to. I'm sorry.
This isn't how it's supposed to go.
Yield. Please. I don't want this.
onLosing: There. That's better. That's right.
*sits down* Worth it. Every bit.
You did good, kid. Real good.
unhinged: You remind me of someone. Before. A long time ago.
I used to be good at this. The winning. It never felt like this.
Eat something after. You look thin.
